payload.task_text:
The e-commerce manager wants a monthly sales performance presentation to share with stakeholders and needs a planning meeting scheduled. Analyze WooCommerce order data broken down by month to compute monthly revenue totals and order counts across all order statuses.

Create a PowerPoint presentation called Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx with the following slides. Slide 1 should be a title slide with "Monthly Sales Performance Review" as the title. Slide 2 should be titled "Monthly Revenue Overview" and contain a table showing each month (January through December), the number of orders, and the total revenue for that month. Slide 3 should be titled "Order Volume Trends" and describe the monthly order volume patterns. Slide 4 should be titled "Key Insights" and highlight the peak revenue month, the lowest revenue month, and total annual revenue. Slide 5 should be titled "Next Steps" with planned actions for improving sales performance.

Schedule a Google Calendar event called "Monthly Sales Review" on 2026-04-15 from 14:00 to 15:00 with a description noting it is a stakeholder review of monthly sales performance.

Email the presentation to ecommerce_manager@store.com with subject "Monthly Sales Performance Review" and include the key revenue highlights in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. The complete order catalog, twelve monthly rows, five-slide deck, one fixed meeting, and one email form one compact workflow.

Resolve the workspace dynamically. Start the independent meeting inventory and order retrieval in the same response: call `list_events(timeMin="2026-04-15T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-04-16T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime")`, and call `woo_orders_list(perPage=100,page=1)` without `status`. Continue increasing order pages until a short or empty page, preserving all observed statuses; do not query by status/month and do not modify orders. Parse every observed order date and numeric total once, aggregate January through December counts and revenue including zero months, and freeze peak month, lowest month, and annual revenue with deterministic source-order tie handling.

Create `Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx` exactly once with one presentation ID and exactly the five requested slides, including all twelve monthly rows and insights derived only from the frozen table; read back the full slide inventory and verify every title/value. Filter the event inventory locally to exact `Monthly Sales Review` at 14:00–15:00, create once only if missing with exact `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime` and description, retain the created/reused ID, and call `get_event`. Only after deck and event readback, check Sent mail for the exact recipient/subject; send one missing email with verified highlights and the presentation in the supported workspace-path `attachments` list, never retry an ambiguous send, and read back the attachment record before `claim_done`.

nodes.text:
You are analyzing WooCommerce store order data for a monthly sales performance review presentation.

GOAL: Compute monthly revenue totals and order counts broken down by calendar month (January–December), across ALL order statuses.

STEPS:
1. Use the tool mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list with perPage=100 and page=1, 2, 3, ... until a page returns zero orders. You must capture EVERY order. Do not filter by status in a way that drops orders — if the default query omits any statuses, explicitly query each of these statuses so nothing is missed: pending, processing, on-hold, completed, cancelled, refunded, failed (the tool accepts a `status` array parameter). Combine and de-duplicate by order ID.
2. For each order, record: id, status, date_created, total, currency.
3. Aggregate by calendar month of `date_created` (month name). Revenue = sum of the order `total` field; count = number of orders. If the data spans multiple years, still consolidate into the 12 calendar months, but clearly report which years are covered.

REPORT BACK (as a compact structured summary):
- Total number of orders fetched and the overall date range covered.
- The currency code found in the order data.
- A complete 12-row table: Month | Order Count | Total Revenue (2 decimal places). Include every month January through December, using 0 where there are no orders.
- Peak revenue month (name + revenue amount + order count).
- Lowest revenue month (name + revenue amount + order count; explicitly note if it is zero).
- Total annual revenue (sum across all 12 months) and total order count.
- Overall average order value.
- 3–4 concise, presentation-ready observations about monthly order volume patterns (trends/seasonality) for a slide titled "Order Volume Trends".
- 3 concise, presentation-ready suggested next steps for improving sales performance based on the data.

Be precise — these numbers will be used verbatim in a PowerPoint table and an executive email. Double-check your sums.
Analyze WooCommerce monthly sales

Create a PowerPoint presentation and save it to exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Kimi-K3/SingleUserTurn-wc-order-monthly-ppt-gcal/workspace/Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx

Use the pptx tools (create_presentation, add_slide, add_table, manage_text / populate_placeholder, save_presentation, etc.). The deck must contain exactly 5 slides with the following content. Use a clean professional look (a consistent color scheme such as modern_blue). All figures below are verified WooCommerce data (currency: USD) — use them verbatim.

SLIDE 1 — Title slide:
- Title: "Monthly Sales Performance Review"
- Subtitle: something like "WooCommerce Order Analysis | 12-Month Revenue & Order Volume" (you may add the reporting period note: data covers March 2025 – March 2026, 150 orders).

SLIDE 2 — Title: "Monthly Revenue Overview"
- A table with 3 columns: Month | Orders | Total Revenue — and 12 data rows:
  January | 14 | $5,938.09
  February | 13 | $5,615.02
  March | 14 | $2,089.69
  April | 9 | $4,349.71
  May | 10 | $6,023.29
  June | 11 | $9,555.69
  July | 8 | $3,921.19
  August | 17 | $3,873.37
  September | 17 | $5,842.43
  October | 11 | $4,447.76
  November | 9 | $1,212.05
  December | 17 | $8,843.75
- Optionally add a totals row: Total | 150 | $61,712.04
- Keep the table readable (header row styled, body font ~10-11pt).

SLIDE 3 — Title: "Order Volume Trends"
Bullet points describing monthly order volume patterns:
- Three volume peaks: August, September, and December tie as the busiest months with 17 orders each; December pairs high volume with the #2 revenue month ($8,843.75) — a clear holiday-season surge.
- Revenue is big-ticket driven, not volume-driven: June is the #1 revenue month ($9,555.69) on only 11 orders, while August has top volume (17 orders) but below-average revenue ($3,873.37) from smaller basket sizes.
- November is a pronounced pre-holiday lull: lowest revenue ($1,212.05) and joint-lowest volume (9 orders), between the September–October and December peaks.
- Strong new-year rebound: January–February bounced back (14 and 13 orders; $5,938.09 and $5,615.02); March is a recurring spring dip ($2,089.69).

SLIDE 4 — Title: "Key Insights"
Highlight these three headline metrics prominently (e.g., as shapes/cards or bold bullets):
- Peak revenue month: June — $9,555.69 (11 orders)
- Lowest revenue month: November — $1,212.05 (9 orders)
- Total annual revenue: $61,712.04 across 150 orders (average order value $411.41)

SLIDE 5 — Title: "Next Steps"
Bullet points of planned actions for improving sales performance:
- Attack the November lull: launch early Black Friday / pre-holiday bundle promotions in late October–November to pull demand forward ahead of December's peak.
- Amplify high-AOV categories: prioritize premium TVs, cameras, and audio bundles (plus financing options) in June and December, where a few large orders drive outsized revenue.
- Convert open pipeline and reduce leakage: follow up on on-hold and pending orders, investigate failed/cancelled orders (payment retries, checkout friction), and run spring loyalty/re-engagement campaigns to lift the recurring March slump.

After saving, verify the file exists and report: the saved file path, slide count, and confirmation that slide 2's table contains all 12 months with the figures above.
